# encrypted fixtures

Read by `tests/oracle/aes.test.ts` (G-AES, read direction). Never edit them by hand: `manifest.json` holds the SHA-256 of every file, and the test fails on any difference.

- `source.pdf` is written byte for byte by `scripts/oracle/encrypted-fixtures.ts` from literals in that script: one page showing `Oracle text` in Helvetica, the Info Title `Oracle fixture` and an XMP metadata stream with the same title.
- The other five files are `source.pdf` encrypted by qpdf 12.4.2 with user password `user` and owner password `owner`: `rc4-40-r2.pdf` (R2, 40-bit RC4), `rc4-128-r3.pdf` (R3, 128-bit RC4), `aes-128-r4.pdf` (R4, AESv2), `aes-128-r4-nometa.pdf` (R4, AESv2, `/EncryptMetadata false`, so the XMP stream stays in cleartext) and `aes-256-r6.pdf` (R6, AESv3). The exact qpdf command line of each file is in `manifest.json` (`made`), with qpdf's `--show-encryption` output (`encryption`).
- `extra/` holds two more AES-256 copies of `source.pdf` by qpdf 12.4.2, read by `tests/unit/crypto/r6-derivation.test.ts` and listed under `extra` in `manifest.json` (the five files above are the set `tests/oracle/aes.test.ts` counts): `extra/aes-256-r5.pdf` (revision 5, `--force-R5`, passwords `user` and `owner`) and `extra/aes-256-r6-nfkc.pdf` (R6, owner password `owner`, user password U+FB01 x U+00AD A U+FF21, recorded as `userPasswordCodePoints`). SASLprep maps that user password to `fixAA`; qpdf hashed the typed form, so the file opens only with the typed password.

`load/` holds the files the encrypted-load tests read (`tests/unit/parser/encryptedLoad.test.ts`, `tests/oracle/encrypted-qdf.test.ts`, `tests/unit/core/decryptedSaveRoutes.test.ts`), listed under `load` in `manifest.json`:

- copies of `source.pdf` by qpdf 12.4.2 with object streams (`--object-streams=generate`): `rc4-40-r2.objstm.pdf`, `rc4-128-r3.objstm.pdf`, `rc4-128-r4.objstm.pdf`, `aes-128-r4.objstm.pdf`, `aes-128-r4-nometa.objstm.pdf` and `aes-256-r6.objstm.pdf`; an R4 RC4 copy without them (`rc4-128-r4.pdf`, `--force-V4`); and `aes-128-r4.empty.pdf`, whose user password is empty (recorded as an empty `userPasswordCodePoints`);
- `signed-aes-128.pdf`: the corpus file `qpdf-signed.pdf` (qpdf test suite, Apache-2.0, see `tests/fixtures/corpus/manifest.json`) encrypted by qpdf 12.4.2 with AESv2 and the passwords `user` and `owner`; qpdf leaves the signature `/Contents` in cleartext;
- `sig-shapes-aes-128-r4.pdf` and `sig-shapes-aes-128-r4-nometa.pdf`: AESv2 copies by qpdf 12.4.2 (passwords `user` and `owner`) of a source that the script writes into its temp directory and never commits. The source has a catalog `/Metadata` stream, a page `/Metadata` stream and four signature-like dictionaries with a literal `/Contents`: no `/Type` with `/ByteRange`, `/Type /Sig` without `/ByteRange`, `/Type /DocTimeStamp` and `/Type /Sig` with `/ByteRange`. The `-nometa` copy is made with `--cleartext-metadata`, so only the catalog's `/Metadata` stream stays in cleartext;
- R4 AESv2 files built byte for byte by the script with node:crypto, with the file key, `/O`, `/U`, `/P` and `/ID` of `aes-128-r4.pdf` (passwords `user` and `owner`) and an IV taken from a SHA-256 of the file and object name: `cons-r4-control.pdf` (every string and stream through `/StdCF`), `cons-r4-stmf-identity.pdf` (`/StmF /Identity`), `cons-r4-strf-identity.pdf` (`/StrF /Identity`), `cons-r4-crypt-identity-stream.pdf` (the content stream has `/Filter [/Crypt]` with `/Name /Identity`), `cons-r4-title-c1.pdf` (Info `/Title` bytes 0x80 to 0x9F) and `cons-r4-title-utf16.pdf` (Info `/Title` bytes `FE FF 00 41 20 14 00 95`). Each has a catalog `/Lang` hex string, an Info `/Title` hex string and an Info `/Author` literal string of octal escapes; qpdf 12.4.2 opens all of them (the manifest holds its `--show-encryption` output).
- Files built byte for byte by the script with the same file key, `/O`, `/U`, `/P` and `/ID` as the R4 files (passwords `user` and `owner`), whose content stream `/Length` is an indirect reference to an integer in an object stream that the cross-reference stream lists after the content stream: `cons-r4-length-in-objstm.pdf` (AESv2, one EOL before `endstream`), `cons-r4-length-in-objstm-2eol.pdf` (AESv2, two EOLs) and `cons-r3-rc4-length-in-objstm-2eol.pdf` (`/V 2 /R 3`, RC4, two EOLs). The content is that of `source.pdf`; qpdf 12.4.2 opens all three and reads the content stream by its `/Length`.

Regenerate with `pnpm run fixtures:encrypted`; verify with `pnpm run fixtures:encrypted:check`. Both need qpdf 12.4.2 (`QPDF=<path>` or `qpdf` on PATH) and refuse any other version. qpdf runs with its test options `--static-id` and `--static-aes-iv`, so the R2, R3 and R4 files are byte-identical on every run and the check compares their SHA-256. qpdf draws the R5 and R6 salts at random, so for `aes-256-r6.pdf` and the two files under `extra/` the check compares `qpdf --decrypt --qdf` of the committed file with the same command on a fresh encryption, and regeneration keeps each committed file when the two agree.

These are test fixtures only: the passwords are public and the RC4 files use encryption that qpdf calls weak (`--allow-weak-crypto`).
